newsitem.title: ITALY: Rome Airport sale to take off this month.
newsitem.headline: Rome Airport sale to take off this month.

text.p: Aeroporti di Roma, the state-controlled company which runs Rome's airports, said it will present its privatisation and development plans on Tuesday.
Italy's bourse watchdog Consob on Friday gave its go-ahead to the privatisation of Aeroporti di Roma, the first Italian airport company to come to the stock market.
Aeroporti di Roma, which is 73.58 percent owned by state industrial holding Iri, will make an initial public share offer (OPV) on July 15 and 16.
A 41 percent stake of the company's capital will be on offer, with the possibility of up to 45 pct through a "green shoe" sale if there is additional demand.
Of the total stake, at least 30 percent will be offered publicly, five percent will be reserved for company employees, and 65 percent will be left for institutional investors.
The price per share will be between 8,000 and 11,000 lire, and will be determined at a shareholders meeting on July 12.
With the offer, Iri's stake in Aeroporti di Roma will fall to around 54 pct.

Lehman Brothers Holdings Plc, Italian bank Imi's LDV Holding B.V., Crediop B.V., UBS Capital B.V. and M.M. Warburg & Co., which indirectly own 25 pct in the company, will also be able to free their stake.

The global coordinator for the offer will be Lehman Brothers International (Europe) and co-global coordinator Cofiri Spa, while the OPV will be coordinated by Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino-Crediop.

Aeroporti di Roma boosted its net profits by 61 percent in 1996 to 90 billion lire and increased its turnover 11 percent to 1.16 trillion lire. The company had asked Consob in March for permission to make the initial share offering.
